text: A website for SmileCare Dental Clinic in Pune: book appointments, services with prices, dentist profiles, emergency dental contact, patient FAQs, and a Marathi version.

@CEO the brief leaves three charter decisions open. Everything it lists stays in scope: booking, priced services, dentist profiles, emergency contact, FAQs and Marathi. The site is one HTML file with no backend.
1. What should 'book appointments' do when a patient submits it?
   Option 1: Embed a third-party booking widget (for example a hosted scheduling service) loaded from a CDN or iframe. Consequence: real slot availability and automatic confirmations. Risk: depends on an outside account and service the Requester must own, and the Marathi version may not translate the widget.
   Option 2: Self-contained slot picker in the page that shows a confirmation screen but stores nothing. Consequence: the fullest-feeling experience for demo and review. Risk: it is not a real booking system, so patients could believe they are booked when the clinic never received anything.
   Option 3: Request form that opens a pre-filled WhatsApp message or email to the clinic, and the clinic confirms by phone. Consequence: works with no backend and real bookings reach the clinic. Risk: the patient gets no instant confirmation, and the clinic must respond promptly or patients drop off.
2. Prices, dentist details and emergency hours are facts only the Requester holds. What do we do about them before launch?
   Option 1: Pause for the Requester to supply real prices, dentist profiles, phone numbers and emergency hours before the site is declared done. Consequence: the finished site carries only verified facts. Risk: the run waits on the Requester, which delays delivery.
   Option 2: Show prices as 'starting from' ranges with a line that final cost is confirmed after examination, and still collect real contact and dentist facts from the Requester. Consequence: lower risk of a wrong exact price and more honest for dental work. Risk: less useful to patients comparing costs, and the Requester must still approve each range.
   Option 3: Build with clearly labelled sample content (marked 'sample') and have the Requester replace it before launch. Consequence: the full site can be reviewed straight away. Risk: sample prices or phone numbers could go live unnoticed and mislead patients, especially in an emergency.
3. How should the Marathi version be delivered and approved?
   Option 1: Same toggle and full parity, but the site is not done until the Requester or a Marathi speaker they name approves the Marathi text. Consequence: higher language quality and trust. Risk: depends on a reviewer being available, which can delay completion.
   Option 2: Consequence: Marathi readers land on Marathi without extra clicks.
   Option 3: Marathi is drafted by the department and marked 'pending native review'. Consequence: both languages ship together and are easy to switch. Risk: unreviewed Marathi may contain wording errors on medical and price content.

@Identity decisions below. Booking is a request form with no backend, prices are ranges, and Marathi ships as a labelled draft. Facts and approvals only the Requester holds stay open inputs shown as marked placeholders and never block done.
1. What should 'book appointments' do when a patient submits it? Request form that opens a pre-filled WhatsApp message or email to the clinic, and the clinic confirms by phone. Consequence: works with no backend and real bookings reach the clinic. Risk: the patient gets no instant confirmation, and the clinic must respond promptly or patients drop off. (It is the only option that needs no backend or outside account and still delivers real requests to the clinic; the trade-off I accept is no instant confirmation, so the page must say the clinic will confirm by phone.)
2. Prices, dentist details and emergency hours are facts only the Requester holds. What do we do about them before launch? Show prices as 'starting from' ranges with a line that final cost is confirmed after examination, and still collect real contact and dentist facts from the Requester. Consequence: lower risk of a wrong exact price and more honest for dental work. Risk: less useful to patients comparing costs, and the Requester must still approve each range. (Starting-from ranges with a 'final cost confirmed after examination' line are the safest honest default for dental pricing; the trade-off is less precise cost comparison, and every price, phone number, dentist detail and emergency hour not yet supplied is a visibly marked placeholder tracked as an open input, so done does not wait on the Requester.)
3. How should the Marathi version be delivered and approved? Marathi is drafted by the department and marked 'pending native review'. Consequence: both languages ship together and are easy to switch. Risk: unreviewed Marathi may contain wording errors on medical and price content. (Full Marathi parity with a toggle ships alongside English and is marked 'pending native review', so done does not wait on a reviewer; the trade-off I accept is possible wording errors until the Requester or a named Marathi speaker approves, which is tracked as an open input.)

@Adaptation the charter is recorded from the brief and the CEO's three decisions. Nothing from the brief is dropped. Propose the workflows that close the done-when items; unsupplied facts stay as marked placeholders and are tracked as open inputs.
@Adaptation Charter valid: statement present, 8 checkable done-when items. Work can start.

@Priority three workflows cover all 8 done-when items for 67 against a budget of 60. I merged emergency contact and FAQ into one section and dropped styling to get this low. Fund W1 and W2 first (45). W3 (Marathi and toggle, 22) is the gap, and the language items cannot close without it. Please either raise the envelope by 7 or tell me which part to cut.

proposal.name: Core English site: booking, services, dentists
proposal.goal_gap: No page exists. Booking, services and dentist items are all open.
proposal.expected_outcome: One HTML file with an English booking request form that opens a pre-filled WhatsApp or email message, a services section with starting-from ranges, and a dentist profiles section. All unsupplied values are visibly marked placeholders. All text is stored in a dictionary keyed by id so Marathi can be added without restructuring.
outputs: smilecare.html with booking, services and dentist sections in English
proposal.completion_check: The file opens with no build step and no backend calls. The form submit builds a WhatsApp or mailto link and the booking section says the clinic confirms by phone. Every service shows a starting-from range and a final-cost-after-examination line. At least one dentist profile exists, with every unsupplied detail marked as a placeholder.

proposal.name: Emergency contact and patient FAQ section
proposal.goal_gap: Emergency contact and FAQ items are open.
proposal.expected_outcome: One section with a prominent emergency contact block (number and hours as marked placeholders) and at least 5 patient FAQs, using the same keyed text dictionary.
outputs: Emergency and FAQ section added to smilecare.html
proposal.completion_check: The emergency block is visible without scrolling into a collapsed element. Its phone number and hours are marked placeholders. The FAQ shows at least 1 question with an answer.

proposal.name: Marathi translation and language toggle
proposal.goal_gap: The language toggle and Marathi parity items are open.
proposal.expected_outcome: A toggle that switches every section, including form labels, placeholders, service lines and FAQs, between English and Marathi. The Marathi view shows a 'pending native review' label, and placeholders are marked in both languages.
outputs: Marathi dictionary and language toggle in smilecare.html
proposal.completion_check: Every dictionary key has both an English and a Marathi value. Toggling changes the text of the booking form, services, dentist profiles, emergency contact and FAQs. The Marathi view shows the 'pending native review' label.

Two non-blocking warnings: booking recipients are empty until the clinic supplies them, and the FAQ and emergency pages carry unreviewed clinical advice. Done. Audit's evidence shows all 8 done-when items pass (7 PASS, 1 PASS_WITH_WARNING), and the mechanical check found no overflow at 360px or 1280px, no JS errors and no broken links. The two warnings are not done-when failures. Empty booking recipients are the already-open contact input. The unreviewed clinical FAQ and emergency text should be handed to the Requester for clinic review, tracked as an open input, and not block done. Open inputs still outstanding: real price ranges, dentist details, clinic phone, WhatsApp and email, emergency number and hours, and Marathi review.

Done: Identity confirmed every done-when item holds, with Audit's evidence. Open inputs for the Requester (not blocking): Real 'starting from' price ranges for each service; Real dentist names, qualifications and profile details; Clinic phone number, WhatsApp number and email address for booking requests; Emergency contact number and emergency hours; Review of the Marathi text by the Requester or a named Marathi speaker.
